A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DCFG research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original counterfactual-generation experiments on CelebA-HQ, EMBED, and MIMIC-CXR, including quantitative results, guidance sensitivity analyses, and generated-image examples.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative and qualitative multi-attribute intervention experiments in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The attribute-split embedding, masked conditioning, weighted denoiser combination, training objective, and DDIM inference remain unchanged. V1 Section 3.2 already permits arbitrary groups and per-attribute guidance with M=K; v3 evaluates these configurations without introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds simultaneous interventions on each pair and all three CelebA-HQ attributes: Smiling, Male, and Young. These extend task requirements beyond v1's single-attribute interventions within an existing dataset. Dataset, domain, and medical-task coverage otherwise remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Standard global CFG, including the unguided weight-1.0 reference, remains the comparison method. The new attribute-wise DCFG rows examine configurations of the existing proposed framework rather than introduce a distinct baseline algorithm.

E3.justification: The new Appendix G experiments compare two-group and per-attribute configurations using symmetric and asymmetric guidance weights under joint interventions. Existing experiments retain their training configurations, fixed evaluation subsets, 1,000-step DDIM sampling, and AUROC, MAE, and LPIPS metrics.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds systematic analyses of grouping granularity and individual guidance weights across all two-attribute combinations and the three-attribute intervention. Tables A.9–A.12 and Figures A.19–A.22 test selective control beyond the earlier two-group weight-sensitivity analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: V1 checklist item 7 explicitly explains that standard deviations and confidence intervals are omitted because multiple training seeds or splits are costly. V3 removes this disclosure with the checklist. Both still report point estimates without uncertainty estimates; an actual change in repeated runs is not established.

E6.justification: Original Tables A.3–A.8 retain their values, while Appendix G adds a substantial family of joint-intervention results. For example, Table A.9 reports MAE 0.227 for global CFG versus 0.189 for two-group DCFG. Benefits are mixed: Table A.10 reports LPIPS 0.138 versus 0.148, respectively. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: Proposition 1, its conditional-independence assumption, and the Appendix B posterior and score derivation are substantively unchanged. Background equations are consolidated and notation clarified. The per-attribute configuration discussed in Appendix G was already included mathematically in v1.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that global CFG amplifies invariant attributes and that DCFG improves intervention control, identity preservation, and reversibility through separate group weights. V3 foregrounds flexibility that v1 already explicitly claimed; the rewritten contribution list and additional evidence do not materially change that scope.

C2.justification: Appendix G adds interpretations of symmetric and asymmetric per-attribute guidance, discusses the all-attributes-intervened case, and acknowledges the computational cost of finer grouping. Existing limitations concerning empirical weight tuning and extensions to higher-resolution models remain.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly states that M groups require M+1 denoiser forward passes, compared with two for global CFG and three for two-group DCFG. The reproducibility statement specifies code release upon acceptance instead of v1's unspecified later release. Appendix C's implementation, hardware, and training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 substantially contracts the cited background, removing works on neural causal identification, counterfactual editing, GANs, and alternative guidance. It adds Rasal et al. (2025), Castro et al. (2020), and Rezende and Mohamed (2015). This revises the breadth of literature coverage, although the specific positioning against Shen et al. and Liu et al. remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, and conclusion receive extensive rewriting. Background subsections are consolidated, experiments are framed as case studies, and limitations are integrated into the conclusion. The checklist is removed, while ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements are introduced.

P2.justification: V3 adds four multi-attribute tables and four qualitative figure grids, with a selected example redisplayed as main Figure 4. It also relocates the reversibility figure, reorders the CelebA qualitative figures, improves Figure 2 labels, changes table headers to 'Guidance configuration,' and adopts different typography and page headers.

improvement.justification: Appendix G supplies useful empirical support for grouping flexibility that v1 claimed but evaluated only through single-attribute interventions. Explicit computational costs also improve transparency. These gains are limited by unchanged uncertainty gaps and overly strong claims that symmetric weights recover grouped results: Table A.12 reports Young AUC 84.7 for global/two-group guidance versus 81.6 for equal per-attribute weights.
